reasons: Deviation classification is sound: the clause has the mutual 'not unreasonably withheld' consent standard but no right for Company to assign to an affiliate or successor on notice, so it fails the fallback ('mutual right to assign to successors with written notice') on a material term rather than merely falling short of preferred wording.

Redline tracks the rule's redline guidance: it preserves the original sentence verbatim and appends only (i) the affiliate/successor carve-out with notice, (ii) the no-assignment-to-competitor limitation, and (iii) confirmation that a Company change of control is not a deemed assignment and gives Contractor no termination/re-pricing right — all limbs of the preferred position.
High changed-character ratio is an artifact of appended provisos to a single short sentence; the existing consent mechanic is untouched, so the edit is effectively minimal.

Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, correctly notes the mutual consent standard is unchanged and explains the change-of-control confirmation; no misstatement of the contract (no separate change-of-control clause exists).
